evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete input mechanism (entering specific fields) rather than only the need to create a game.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a particular technical mechanism (URL-based invitation) instead of the underlying need to invite participants.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a specific UI widget (single multi-line text field) rather than the need to provide an item to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States an information need (visibility of items) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the capability needed (choose an item) without dictating UI/technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to add items; does not prescribe how it must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the required user capability (edit) without solution-level constraints.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to remove an item; no concrete UI/technical mechanism is mandated.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired behavior/outcome (reveal estimates early) rather than implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific algorithm/aggregation method (average) rather than the need to finalize an estimate.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Dictates UI element behavior (a specific field auto-filled) and a concrete rule, instead of the underlying need to speed acceptance when unanimous.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the need to record the agreed estimate without prescribing technical/UI specifics beyond the basic action.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user need (re-estimation) without implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific source/format (spreadsheet) as the mechanism rather than the general need to bulk-load stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete interaction/technical approach (copy/paste from spreadsheet) instead of the underlying need to add multiple stories quickly.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to find prior games without prescribing UI/technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States an information need (see transcript) without specifying storage/export mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific output format (HTML file) rather than the need to export/save a transcript.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific storage/export format (CSV) instead of the stakeholder need to export data for processing.

evaluations.evidence: so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Includes a concrete implementation/storage detail (no longer stored) rather than focusing on the need to remove a game and its data from user perspective.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete data fields and entry mechanism rather than the need to register for access.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific authentication mechanism/credentials rather than the need to authenticate.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: States the need to update account information without prescribing how.

evaluations.evidence: so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Mentions a concrete storage/implementation outcome (no longer stored) rather than focusing purely on the user need to delete the account.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user need (localized time display) without prescribing implementation.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific delivery mechanism (email) rather than the broader need to recover access.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Overly prescribes specific estimation scales/values (solution choice) rather than the need to configure an estimation scale.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Imposes a concrete numeric limit (15) which is a solution/constraint choice rather than expressing the underlying scalability need.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific UI/technical mechanisms (URL page, entering name) rather than the need to join a game.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States an information need without prescribing how it is displayed.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses visibility need; no solution details mandated.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired feedback/timeliness without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Specifies required behavior (simultaneous reveal after all voted) rather than implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: Defines a rule/need about when changes are allowed; does not prescribe technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: States an information need without specifying storage format or UI components.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a transparency need; no solution prescription.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific solution mechanism and parameter (a two-minute countdown timer) rather than the general need to timebox discussion.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific mechanism and behavior (two-minute timer auto-reset trigger) rather than the underlying need to prepare timing for next round.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to review prior information; 'scroll back' is not a concrete widget/implementation mandate here.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: States a consistency need (stable ordering) without prescribing how ordering is implemented.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Defines a business rule about allowed changes; no implementation details prescribed.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes concrete UI elements and placement (small thumbnail photo displayed near cards) rather than the need to personalize participants.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete technical standards/implementation choices rather than the stakeholder need (e.g., broad accessibility/compatibility).

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: States a documentation/understanding need without prescribing technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Directly prescribes a technical mechanism (database indexes) instead of the need (fast queries/performance).

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific technical platform targets (exact browser versions) rather than the general compatibility need.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Mandates a specific standard (W3C guidelines) as the solution approach rather than stating the accessibility need in problem terms.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a performance need without prescribing implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific technical encoding/standard (Unicode) rather than the underlying need to support multiple languages/characters.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: States a user-facing need (predictable URLs) without dictating specific routing/format rules.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user experience need without prescribing specific UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: States a stakeholder need about privacy/anonymization; does not prescribe a specific anonymization algorithm or storage format.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Expresses an information need (usage metrics) without prescribing how metrics are collected or displayed.
